messages:
maria: Hey team — I put up the draft PRD for the Minimum Viable Dedicated Tier (MVDT) with a new "Burst-aware autoscale" flow. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/mvdt-burst-autoscale :point_up: Would like feedback on SLA targets and the acceptance criteria by EOW.

jonathan: skimmed it. overall looks solid. a couple notes: we need clearer throughput units (rps vs tokens/sec) per GPU. customers keep asking for tokens/sec guarantees. also can we quantify burst headroom?

maria: good call. current draft uses tokens/sec at 512 context. suggested baseline 50k tokens/sec per V100-equivalent GPU, burst headroom 2x for up to 5m. open to adjusting if runtime disagrees.

kevin: 50k tokens/sec sounds generous for a 3B model on a V100. for larger models we'll need per-model profiles. propose we add a table in PRD: model_family -> baseline_tokens/s -> burst_multiplier -> p99_latency_target.

kevin: also: cold-starts are the real pain. acceptance criteria should force a max cold-start to warm state for a pinned model <= 30s for dedicated pools, otherwise we need pre-warm steps.

oliver: customer voice: several customers asked for predictable billing when burst exceeds commit. they want a 5-minute free burst window before metering, or at least explicit notification. sales is seeing churn risk if burst billing surprises them.

amanda: +1 from sales. recommend 'grace window' in PRD: first 5 minutes of burst per day free, thereafter billed at burst-rate. need legal & finance signoff but include as ask.

kevin: that billing behavior affects autoscale policy — if we give free burst, we should allow short spikes without scale-out to avoid billing churn. propose autoscale target uses 85% sustained util for scale up but treats 5m spikes as 'allowed' without scaling until crossing spike-policy.

jonathan: implementation note: runtime can support two modes: "eager-scale" (scale immediately when util>threshold) and "spike-tolerant" (delay scale for burst_window). spike-tolerant cheaper but risks queueing. need SLO tradeoffs doc.

sophia: from SRE: acceptance criteria we should include faulting behavior & graceful degradation. if pool runs out of capacity during burst, we must: 1) route to fallback model (compatible smaller quantized model) with <2s added latency, 2) emit an incident metric and customer notice.

sophia: also add ops runbook steps for manual spillover to dedicated cold pool and rollback path for canary.

maria: adding that. for the fallback model path, we need a model compatibility matrix in PRD and the routing policy: prefer same-region fallback, then cross-region.

kevin: sample autoscale config to include in PRD: 
```
policy: spike_tolerant
min_replicas: 1
max_replicas: 16
scale_up_threshold: 85
burst_window: 300s  # 5 minutes
scale_cooldown: 120s
fallback_model: small-quant-3b
```

jonathan: + add metrics to acceptance criteria: 99.95% uptime for dedicated pools (per-month), p99 inference latency <= target in table for baseline load, and <1% requests routed to fallback in normal ops (excluding known load-tests).

maria: draft acceptance checklist I added to PRD (pulling items together): 
- SLA: 99.95% per-customer uptime for dedicated pools (monthly)
- Baseline throughput guarantees per model family (table)
- Burst headroom: 2x baseline for up to 5m with grace window behavior
- Cold-start: pinned models warm in <=30s
- Fallback: compatible model activated with <2s added latency when capacity exhausted
- Observability: per-route cost/latency, burst-metering events, and per-customer capacity alerts
- Rollout: canary to 5 customers (non-production) -> 10 customers -> full GA

oliver: can we add acceptance criterion for documentation: clear docs for customers showing billing examples (with/without free burst) and recommended request patterns? customers read docs first.

maria: yes — documentation & sample config must be approved before GA.

amanda: would like an explicit "customer opt-in" flag for free-burst behavior per account. not everyone wants surprises.

kevin: ops-wise, opt-in makes sense. add per-account policy and explicit header to API: `X-Redwood-Burst-OptIn: true` to opt into grace window.

jonathan: please also add acceptance tests: synthetic load generator that runs 2x baseline for 6m and asserts billing meter behavior and fallback routing. include infra task to wire test into CI.

sophia: we should simulate regional outage: test that routing fallback to cross-region respects data residency (only if account allows cross-region). include that in edge-cases.

maria: great list. last ask: can runtime/infra owners estimate effort and propose MVE (min viable engineering) slice we can ship in 6 weeks? kevin/jonathan can we get rough estimates tomorrow? :eyes:

kevin: rough: MVE = core autoscale + burst_window policy + fallback routing + simple billing hook ~ 4 wks for runtime+infra engineering (2 engs) + 2 wks for qa/rollout docs (1 sec, 1 doc writer). depends on pre-existing model profiles.

jonathan: infra dependencies: need metrics pipeline hooks and per-account policy storage — ~1 wk infra work. can parallelize.

maria: thanks. I'll update PRD with actions and owners. planning a short sync Thu 11a to finalize acceptance criteria. :calendar:

deploy-bot: Document updated by maria: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/mvdt-burst-autoscale (version 3)

amanda: :thumbsup: will loop in finance for the billing examples.

oliver: I'll flag two customers who want early access — will add names to the PRD.

maria: perfect. if no objections, we'll freeze acceptance criteria after Thu sync and start implementation next week. :rocket:
